source.title: Dynamical memristors for higher-complexity neuromorphic computing

confidence_rationale: Top-venue review giving strong evidence memristive media natively INSTANTIATE persistent state, history-dependent plasticity, multi-timescale dynamics, oscillation and attractor/threshold transitions. But mapping_fidelity is low -- device-physics capability mapped by analogy onto REE's abstract primitive list with no physical REE substrate -- and it is silent on auditability and hard safety gating.
failure_signatures: The higher-order dynamics the review praises are emergent products of stochastic ionic/filamentary processes, so 'native instantiation' and 'uncontrolled variability/drift' are two faces of the same physics.
Offers no verification, auditability, or hard-gating mechanism -- only richer dynamics.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Memristors naturally embody higher-order dynamics through internal electrophysical processes -- volatile/non-volatile state, short/long-term plasticity, threshold/spiking, self-oscillation, chaos, and locally-active negative-differential-resistance -- so a single device can replace elaborate digital circuitry.
mapping.ree_translation: Speaks to Q-066's INSTANTIATION axis: memristive media plausibly instantiate (not merely approximate) persistent state, history-dependent deformation, multi-timescale dynamics, oscillatory propagation, and attractor transitions from the ARC-089 primitive list.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Device-physics capability in a benchmark crossbar is not a demonstration that REE's specific primitives (simulated-action deformation, offline reintegration) survive in this medium, nor that REE's hard safety-gate is realizable here; no physical REE substrate exists to measure.
mapping.source_context: Device-physics review of memristor dynamics for neuromorphic computing.

confidence_components.notes: POST-V5 derivation against device specs, not measurement of any REE substrate.
